page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core tests. Multi-core CPU performance, Passmark CPU scores, and Geekbench multi-core metrics fall within the average tier. Memory performance is a notable tradeoff; while cached small-block read bandwidth is average, the Passmark memory score and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression are categorized in the bottom 25%, reflecting the low memory-to-core ratio.

Due to its high compute-to-memory ratio, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for CPU-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints. It is suitable for tasks such as web serving, software compilation, and lightweight batch processing. However, it is poorly suited for memory-intensive databases or large-scale data analytics due to the 8.0 GB memory constraint.
